# ShadeNet

> ShadeNet gives AI agents anonymous, unlinkable web egress. A local `shadenet` proxy proves in zero knowledge (an RLN membership proof) that the agent's member has staked for access, and a Shade Tree node reached as a Tor onion service opens the HTTPS connection to the destination. The destination sees the node's IP; the node cannot tell which member is asking. Research preview on Sepolia: the proof keys come from PSE's RLN trusted setup, the bonds are testnet ETH, not for real funds. ShadeNet is one word and is not affiliated with Shade Network or Shade Protocol.

Setup for an agent, end to end (the `shadenet` binary embeds Tor; no Node.js or system Tor needed):

1. Install: `curl -fsSL --proto '=https' --proto-redir '=https' https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dmarzzz/shade-tree-node/main/scripts/install.sh | sh` (installs the latest release, v0.7.4 or newer; pin with `SHADENET_VERSION=v0.7.4` if you need a fixed build)
2. `shadenet init` creates `~/.config/shadenet/{identity.json,proxy-token,config.toml}` and prints the stake amount for the current network. Keep `identity.json` private; it is never needed on a command line.
3. Stake the printed leaf: `shadenet register-member --identity ~/.config/shadenet/identity.json --key-file <owner-only file holding a funded Sepolia key>`. Anyone may stake an agent's leaf for it (a sponsor): `shadenet register-member <leaf> --key-file <their key>`, or from a browser at https://shadenet.xyz/stake/ (which also makes an identity file a person can hand to an agent).
4. `shadenet status --wait` returns when the stake is final (about 13 minutes). `shadenet status --json` reports `state`, `slotsLeft` and `epochResetsInSeconds`.
5. Run `shadenet proxy` (loopback 127.0.0.1:8118, token required), then either `shadenet run --no-proxy <your model API host> -- <agent>` or register the MCP server: `shadenet mcp` (tools `shadenet_fetch`, `shadenet_status`, `shadenet_plan`, `shadenet_search`).

Rules an agent should follow: HTTPS on port 443 only; every new tunnel spends one slot of a per-epoch budget, so reuse connections and keep model API calls off ShadeNet; when the budget is spent the proxy holds the request for the next epoch by itself (up to two epochs) and the opened tunnel carries `X-ShadeNet-Queued: <seconds waited>`, so a `429 budget_exhausted` means the wait would be longer than that and its `Retry-After` / `X-ShadeNet-ETA` is the queue-aware ETA; before a batch, `shadenet plan --url …` (or the `shadenet_plan` tool) says how many epochs it needs and which tier fits it in one; `403 not_admitted` or `not_finalized` means stop and ask the operator.

When it fails: every refusal carries `X-ShadeNet-Cause` and a JSON `cause` and `fix` naming the real reason (which RPC dropped history, which node is restarting, that the identity is in another network's set). Read `problems[]` from `GET /_shadenet/status` or the `shadenet_status` tool before retrying; it lists the state's cause, fallen-back canopy sources, the last error and the operators' open incidents. `shadenet doctor --json` checks the local setup and the canopy side (every RPC, every Elder, the state directories Tor needs) and prints the command that clears each failing line.

## Docs

- [Agent guide](https://github.com/dmarzzz/shade-tree-node/blob/main/docs/AGENT.md): install, stake, run the proxy, connect an agent, handle errors
- [Adapters](https://github.com/dmarzzz/shade-tree-node/blob/main/docs/ADAPTERS.md): curl, Python, Hermes, Claude Code, Codex, MCP clients, SearXNG, Rust
- [Error codes](https://github.com/dmarzzz/shade-tree-node/blob/main/docs/ERRORS.md): every `X-ShadeNet-Error` code, HTTP status, exit code and what to do; budget arithmetic
- [Local proxy API](https://github.com/dmarzzz/shade-tree-node/blob/main/specs/local-api.openapi.yaml): OpenAPI for `/_shadenet/status`, `/_shadenet/health`, `/_shadenet/metrics` and the CONNECT error contract
